entries.speaker: Coroner

entries.text: Mrs. Skur, I hope I'm not disturbing you.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: You have a lot of nerve coming here.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Skur

entries.text: Your husband-- you know he's not dead.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: How dare you.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Skur

entries.text: Your husband was discredited in order to cover up a crime-- a crime that was committed upon him, against his will.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: Whatever was done to my husband, you're a part of it.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Skur

entries.text: According to v.a. Records, your husband underwent surgery for war injuries. So did two other men he worked with at the state department. But the surgeries that they received-- it wasn't what they thought it was. It had nothing to do with their war injuries.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: Then what was it?
entries.speaker: Mrs. Skur

entries.text: It's called xenotransplantation. It's, uh, the grafting of another species into the human body. It's a procedure that Nazi doctors experimented with during the war, and I believe that they continued their work here, using your husband and these other two men as unwitting test subjects. I want to expose what was done to your husband, mrs. Skur. I can't do that unless I have his help.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: Get in. Just get in.
entries.speaker: Roy Cohn

entries.text: [ dog barking ]

entries.text: Ed? Oh, God. Are you all right?
entries.speaker: Mrs. Skur

entries.text: I told you not to come down here.
entries.speaker: Edward Skur

entries.text: That FBI agent came back.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Skur

entries.text: [ panting, gagging ] I'm getting worse.
entries.speaker: Edward Skur

entries.text: He says he wants to help you.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Skur

entries.text: It's too late to help me.
entries.speaker: Edward Skur

entries.text: No.

entries.text: I can't help myself anymore.

entries.text: [ gagging ]

entries.text: You sit there.

entries.text: Leave us alone.

entries.speaker: Roy Cohn

entries.text: Leave us.

entries.text: In 1945, at the time of the first conference... To map out the peace after the second world war, there lived within the soviet orbit 180 million people. Lined up on the antitotalitarian side at that time... Were 1,625,000,000 people. Today, mr. Dales, just seven years later, there are 800 million people... Under the absolute domination of soviet Russia-- an increase of over 400%. On our side, the figure has shrunk to around 500 million. In other words, in less than seven years... The odds have changed from nine-to-one in our favor... To eight-to-five against us. The threat of global communist domination... Is a reality that can be ignored... Only at the risk of our own annihilation.
entries.speaker: J. Edgar Hoover

entries.text: The men we arrested weren't communists.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: If we are to defeat the enemy, we must use their tools. We must go further! We must do those things which even our enemies would be ashamed to do. It is only through strength... That we can make our enemies fear us... And thereby ensure our own survival. You have one chance, mr. Dales, to save yourself, to demonstrate that you have the strength... To serve your country.
entries.speaker: J. Edgar Hoover

entries.text: Make your meeting with Skur. Let him think you're alone. Put him at ease. We'll be in when the time is right.
entries.speaker: Bill Mulder

entries.text: Was this why you came to see me, mr. Mulder-- make me your stalking-horse?
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: I follow my orders.
entries.speaker: Bill Mulder

entries.text: I might need that.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: We want him alive.
entries.speaker: Bill Mulder

entries.text: There ya go.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: I turned the lights off out front. Just pull the door shut when you go.
entries.speaker: Bartender

entries.text: Okay. Thanks for your help.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: Anything to help out the Bureau.
entries.speaker: Bartender

entries.text: Did you come here to kill me, or to save me?
entries.speaker: Edward Skur

entries.text: I'm here to help you, just like I told your wife.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: My wife is dead. I'm dead too, inside, because of this thing they put in me. For what-- to turn me into some kind of killing machine, or just to see what would happen? They're not coming, you know. They wanted me to kill you, or you wouldn't be here. You're part of their test now too.
entries.speaker: Edward Skur

entries.text: I don't want to kill you.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: I know.

entries.text: I can't believe my father threw in with these men. [ sighs ] he let them dictate his conscience.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Oh, don't fool yourself. None of us are free to choose. I was ruined for my insubordination. You keep digging through the X-Files, and they'll bury you too.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: Skur died saying my father's name. Why?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I haven't the faintest idea.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: There was, uh-- there's one thing you didn't explain. It was... How Skur was able to get away; how he was able to live in obscurity for the last 38 years.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Thirty-eight years? My God. Well, I kept hearing things through the years, you know. People tell me things. I heard that he was dead, that he was kept in some secret lab while they finished up the experiment.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: [ chuckling ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: I even thought that maybe-- maybe some poor, innocent bastard-- somebody with a conscience-- might have let him go.
entries.speaker: Arthur Dales

entries.text: Why would anyone do that? Why let a killer go free?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: In the hope that by letting him live, the truth of the crimes that were committed... Against him and the others... Might someday be exposed.
